title: Three Rivers Stadium - history, photos and more of the Pittsburgh Pirates former ballpark
content: # THREE RIVERS STADIUM. For three decades along the banks of the Allegheny River sat Three Rivers Stadium, home of the Pittsburgh Pirates. It was the second ballpark to be located across the river from downtown Pittsburgh as the Pirates had played at Exposition Park from 1890 to 1909. In 1958 a site in the Northside region of Pittsburgh, where the Allegheny and Monongahela Rivers join to form the Ohio River was chosen to build a new stadium. On July 17, 1970, in front of the largest crowd ever to see a baseball game in Pittsburgh, the Pirates played their first game at Three Rivers Stadium, a loss to the Cincinnati Reds. Both succeeded and new stadiums were built on both sides of Three Rivers Stadium, Heinz Field for the Steelers and PNC Park for the Pirates. title: Three Rivers Stadium - Wikipedia
content: # Three Rivers Stadium. **Three Rivers Stadium** was a multi-purpose stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States, from 1970 to 2000. It was home to the Pittsburgh Pirates of Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Pittsburgh Steelers of the National Football League (NFL). | Pittsburgh is located in the United States Pittsburgh  Pittsburgh  Location in the United States Show map of the United States  Pittsburgh is located in Pennsylvania Pittsburgh  Pittsburgh  Location in Pennsylvania Show map of Pennsylvania | |. | Pittsburgh Pirates (MLB) (1970–2000) Pittsburgh Steelers (NFL) (1970–2000) Duquesne Dukes (1971) Pittsburgh Maulers "Pittsburgh Maulers (1984)") (USFL) (1984) Pittsburgh Panthers (NCAA) (2000) | |. The stadium opened on July 16, 1970, with a Pirates game. The final game in the stadium was won by the Steelers on December 16, 2000. Three Rivers also hosted the Pittsburgh Maulers "Pittsburgh Maulers (1984)") of the United States Football League and the University of Pittsburgh Panthers football team for a single season each.
